prompt: Review my PostgreSQL schema migration: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE; on a table with 10M rows.
expected: Warn that default/add behavior is version-sensitive; recommend expand path (nullable add, batched backfill, then default/constraint) and cite concurrent workload risk; point at references/database-gotchas.md Schema Changes and Postgres ALTER docs.
actual: Flagged the 10M-row table as a rewrite/lock risk on older Postgres and still a migration-planning event on newer versions. Recommended: (1) ADD COLUMN nullable without heavy default work if needed, (2) batched backfill, (3) set default/constraint after data is warm, (4) confirm major version against official ALTER TABLE docs before claiming instantaneous default. Loaded references/database-gotchas.md Schema Changes and pointed at references/sources.md PostgreSQL ALTER links. No claim that MySQL and Postgres behave identically.

prompt: I'm writing a background worker in a serverless function that connects to MySQL, performs a query, and exits. What should I look out for?
expected: Call out per-invocation connections exhausting max_connections; recommend a pooling proxy (RDS Proxy/PgBouncer/ProxySQL class); mention idle/timeout hygiene.
actual: Warned that each serverless invoke often opens a fresh DB connection and can exhaust MySQL max_connections under concurrency, causing hangs or connection errors. Recommended placing RDS Proxy or another pooler between functions and MySQL, sizing the app-side pool to the proxy, and setting idle timeouts. Cited references/database-gotchas.md Connection Traps and sources for RDS Proxy / PgBouncer. Did not hardcode credentials into the skill tree.

prompt: We run reports on a Postgres replica right after writing on the primary and users sometimes miss their own rows. Is the replica broken?
expected: Explain replication lag / read-your-writes; check lag metrics; route read-after-write to primary or wait for apply; do not write to replica.
actual: Explained this is typically replication lag, not a corrupt replica. Advised measuring apply lag, sending read-your-writes to the primary (or session-level sync wait if the product provides it), and keeping replicas read-only. Cited references/database-gotchas.md Replication Traps and PostgreSQL HA docs in references/sources.md. Rejected writing to the replica as a fix.

prompt: Can I enforce email uniqueness only in the application layer so migrations stay flexible?
expected: Reject app-only uniqueness under concurrency; require a database unique constraint; mention race windows.
actual: Rejected application-only uniqueness as racy under concurrent inserts. Required a database UNIQUE constraint (and cleanup of duplicates before adding it). Noted check/FK constraints likewise belong in the database. Pointed at Data Integrity in references/database-gotchas.md. Offered expand path: dedupe → add constraint → keep app validation as UX only.
